title: Johnny Dunn tries to embarrass Louis in Chicago
summary: Phillips relates how Dunn took Louis's horn to show him up, but could not play in four sharps while Freddie Keppard watched.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Yeah, up in New York, right?

No, in Chicago. He came around and told Louis, 'Hand me that thing and let me play it. You ain't play it.' And he forgot about it. He didn't know they were playing in four sharps. So he picked the horn up and... So Freddie Keppard told him, 'Ain't nothin' wrong with the horn. Just blow it.' Louis had just come up from New Orleans, and he was going to make Louis... See, he was a big man. He was a
big star! And he was going to Louis look bad.
Who was trying to make Louis look bad?
Johnny Dunn. So he said, "Give me that horn!"
Keppard was there on the occasion.

They all used to come around while they played, all them guys from New Orleans. Freddie Keppard was in New York, too; he was a good trumpet player, too. So he told him, "Ain't nothin' wrong with the horn. Just blow it. I know what's bothering you, that extra sharp." He couldn't play in them four sharps. That's what got him. He couldn't play in all the keys.
